1.d4 d5 2.c4 c6 3.cxd5 cxd5 4.Nc3 Nf6 5..strategy: Develops the bishop outside the pawn chain before e3 can shut it in, taking the diagonal towards c7 and b8 and control of e5. It is the natural way to use the extra move, and Black has to decide how to match it.

Mirrors the bishop and completes a fully symmetrical position in which every piece is well placed and neither side has a target. Black has reached equality by simple means; whoever wants more than a draw has to unbalance the position.
1.d4 d5 2.c4 c6 3.cxd5 cxd5 4.Nc3 Nf6 5..name: Slav Defence: Exchange Variation, Symmetrical Line
